name: Utah
summary: Utah was the first state to legalize plug-in solar. A certified device of up to 1,200 watts can be plugged in without your utility's approval, an interconnection agreement, or any fee.
watt_cap_note: Maximum power output of the device. The statute does not say whether this is AC or DC; trackers read it as inverter (AC) output.
certification: Must be certified by a nationally recognized testing laboratory. The bill text references UL 1741 (the inverter standard); it predates UL 3700.

utility.fees: Utilities may not charge fees or require extra equipment.
utility.net_metering: Not eligible. Power you export earns no credit.

renters: Not addressed. Your lease controls, so ask your landlord in writing.
hoa: Not addressed. HOA or condo rules can still restrict placement.
notes: The utility is not liable for damage or injury caused by the device.
open_questions: Signing date (March 25, 2025) comes from secondary sources and is not in the enrolled text.
